$comment: Glossary lint for the message catalogs (docs/i18n-glossary.md, docs/i18n.md). node scripts/i18n-check.mjs fails when a message in a rule's locale and surfaces contains one of its forbidden words (a plain substring, so Hebrew prefixes such as ה, ל, מ and ש are covered). A genuine exception names the rule and the message as <surface>:<namespace>.<key> and says why; an exception that matches nothing fails too. A rule with "whenSource" (and optionally "unlessSource"), case-insensitive regular expressions, checks only the messages whose English source matches "whenSource" and not "unlessSource": the English decides which role a word names, so forms that are right elsewhere (the tutor's מנחה) fail where it names the other role.

rules.use: המנחה (מנחה ה-AI where the AI nature matters, מנחה הלומדים as the admin job name)
rules.why: the learner-facing tutor (the companion) is המנחה, owner decisions 7 and 16
המפקח is the staff-side supervisor and appears only in admin; learners see one helper, המנחה (owner decision 16)

in admin המנחה is the learner-facing tutor and המפקח the staff-side supervisor (owner decisions 7 and 16). Where the English names a supervisor or supervision and no companion or tutor, a מנחה form can only mean the supervisor, so every declined form fails: מנחה, המנחה, למנחה, מנחים, המנחים, מנחי, מנחות

rules.use: המנחה (plural המנחים; מנחה הלומדים as the admin job name)
rules.why: the same two roles the other way round: where the English names the companion or tutor and no supervisor or supervision, a מפקח form (המפקח, למפקח, המפקחים, מפקחי) names the wrong role (owner decisions 7 and 16)
placed out is never דולג (owner decision 7)
a policy scope is never היקף (owner decision 7)
owner decision 7; replay is הפעלה חוזרת
cohort, artifact, ledger and remediation have Hebrew terms (owner decision 7)

exceptions.reason: a local clock time that a daylight-saving change skips, not a placement
